Analysis complete. Here's a summary of what was produced:

## Deliverables

**`case-studies/tokio-broadcast/modeling-brief.md`** — Primary handoff document for spec generation
**`case-studies/tokio-broadcast/analysis-report.md`** — Detailed audit trail

## Key Findings

**5 Bug Families** identified from 13 bug-fix commits, 15 deeply-read GitHub issues (7 confirmed bugs, 5 excluded as user error):

| Family | Historical Bugs | Priority | Model-Checkable |
|--------|----------------|----------|-----------------|
| 1. **Channel Close Lifecycle** — dual-flag close state (tail.closed vs num_tx), re-open on subscribe, close sentinel issues | 3 | HIGH | Yes |
| 2. **Waiter Notification Protocol** — lost wakeups, memory leaks, deadlocks from waker re-entrancy, O(n²) re-registration | 4 | HIGH | Yes |
| 3. **Slot Value Lifecycle / rem Counter** — unsoundness (RUSTSEC-2025-0023), panic on drop during concurrent sends | 2 | MEDIUM | Yes |
| 4. **Position Wraparound / Lag Arithmetic** — non-wrapping operations at u64 boundary, lag recovery edge cases | 1+2 code findings | MEDIUM | Yes |
| 5. **Reference Counting** — ordering subtleties in num_tx/rx_cnt/rem | 1 | LOW | No (loom) |

**New code findings** (not previously known):
- `Receiver::len()` (line 1167) uses non-wrapping subtraction — debug-mode panic at u64 wraparound
- `Receiver::drop` (line 1563) uses non-wrapping comparison — skips cleanup at u64 wraparound
- `is_closed()` vs `recv_ref` check different close state — observable inconsistency window
- `Sender::len()` binary search can see non-monotonic rem values from concurrent receivers
